quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Bakelite results briefing Q&A: FY2026 Q1 Financial Results Briefing Q&A Summary (08-03-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Q1 results briefing Q&A summary, quarter ended June 2026; presenter Managing Executive Officer Toshiya Hirai) on encapsulants: the main growth driver is AI-related demand, especially power device applications, with data-center expansion giving strong momentum; the biggest factor is demand growth as data centers expand globally, increasing the use of power semiconductors around GPUs and driving volumes, while the company's track record in high-reliability fields leads to preferential adoption and rising demand for high thermal conductivity is a tailwind. Demand for advanced applications such as MUF has also started to grow. Chinese smartphone-related demand has paused temporarily, but automotive, communications and home-appliance applications remain broadly firm; demand in China is expanding further and automotive recovery in Southeast Asia is more pronounced. April-June growth was consistently strong across the quarter, with no sign of a significant decline in July; management says the top priority is stable, reliable supply.

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Bakelite results briefing Q&A: FY2026 Q1 Financial Results Briefing Q&A Summary (08-03-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Q1 results briefing Q&A summary) on capacity, pricing and competition: the additional encapsulant capacity expansion in China is expected to require less than JPY 5.0 billion, with exchange-rate moves (yen depreciation, renminbi appreciation) a factor. The encapsulant price revision for June shipments will be reflected from Q2, but price increases are meant to reflect raw-material costs and, given competition and customer pricing pressure, prices cannot keep rising easily; business profit should be judged together with volume growth, mix and production rationalisation. Management says its accumulated data on manufacturing recipes and customer use and its long-established local-for-local structure in China let it respond to customers as fast as or faster than improving Chinese local players, and it does not believe they will catch up easily, though competition is expected to intensify.
quarterly_data.figure: China encapsulant capacity expansion investment less than JPY 5.0 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Bakelite results briefing Q&A: FY2026 Q1 Financial Results Briefing Q&A Summary (08-03-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Q1 results briefing Q&A summary) on the acquisition of Kyocera's chemical business: integration preparations are progressing and the share transfer agreement remains on track to become effective on October 30; the business is expected to contribute to earnings from November, but this is not in the earnings forecast and is essentially an upside factor; the profit impact cannot yet be quantified because the two companies' accounting systems and processes still need alignment.
quarterly_data.figure: Share transfer effective October 30; earnings contribution from November (not in forecast)

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Bakelite results briefing Q&A: FY2026 Q1 Financial Results Briefing Q&A Summary (08-03-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Q1 results briefing Q&A summary) on strategic mobility products: sales grew 36% year on year and 18% quarter on quarter. Encapsulants for fixing motor magnets were the main driver, up more than 40% on strong HEV demand in Japan and North America and higher sales to local Chinese customers; ECU encapsulants (adopted mainly in Europe) are recovering, with further growth expected from around July or August; power-module encapsulants benefit from strong HEV demand in Japan and North America and growing sales to local Chinese customers; stator encapsulants are being adopted more widely in robotics, including actuators in joints such as hands.
quarterly_data.figure: Strategic mobility products +36% YoY, +18% QoQ; motor magnet encapsulants up more than 40%

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Bakelite results briefing Q&A: FY2026 Q1 Financial Results Briefing Q&A Summary (08-03-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Q1 results briefing Q&A summary) on company-wide and other segments: the initial JPY 2.0 billion negative impact assumed for the Middle East situation and higher raw-material prices was a preliminary assumption; how far these factors will affect results is still unclear, naphtha prices temporarily rose to unexpectedly high levels, and volumes risk a rebound from inventory adjustments after some front-loaded demand, so the full year remains uncertain, but given progress in passing through price increases and firm demand growth management does not see an overly pessimistic view as warranted. High-Performance Plastics: the 10% business profit margin came largely from completing the North American structural reform (including exiting unprofitable businesses) and from growing sales of new and high-margin products such as COPLUS; the reform's benefits are expected to continue, though higher volumes could raise fixed costs at some stages; some front-loaded demand occurred but Asia remains firm, while Europe is being monitored. Cost pass-through has progressed in products such as heat dissipation sheets. Quality of Life: pharmaceutical packaging is uncertain, and food packaging and some industrial functional materials may have seen front-loaded demand on naphtha-availability concerns.
quarterly_data.figure: Initial JPY 2.0 billion negative impact assumption; High-Performance Plastics business profit margin 10%
